interface.shortDescription: Primary local execution, testing, desktop, and agent bridge for heaven
interface.longDescription: Use the user's private Heaven Local Bridge as the default and exclusive path for computer work on heaven. Durable implementation lives on repository main; the heaven-bridge branch is the live queue/result transport only. Worker v4 adds bounded semantic Windows UI Automation on top of structured filesystem/process execution, screenshots, coordinate desktop input, window control, controller checkpoints, local-agent dispatch, and token-efficient result handling. Version 0.6.0 supports UIA tree/find/focus/invoke/value/toggle/select/expand/collapse actions, fails closed on ambiguous or truncated mutation searches, blocks password ValuePattern writes, and requires explicit relay opt-in for non-secret UIA text. Agent Control/local worker fabric remains the preferred parallel-work path when Codex quota is unavailable.
defaultPrompt: Use Heaven Local Bridge for this heaven computer task. Do not use Remote Desktop Commander unless I explicitly authorize it.
Run this repository build/test/debug workflow locally on heaven using main as implementation truth and the heaven-bridge branch only as transport.
Coordinate parallel local work on heaven through Agent Control/worker fabric when useful; if Codex quota is unavailable, continue with structured bridge actions and local workers instead of stopping.

name: heaven-local-bridge
description: Primary local-control and development bridge for the user's heaven worker: secure filesystem, code build/test execution, persistent dev processes, binary transfer, search, shell, concurrent jobs, screenshots and desktop control, status/cancellation, controller checkpoints, local agents, worker-fabric offloading, and token-efficient result handling through its declared GitHub connected-app relay. Includes dedicated code-execution, desktop-control, and local-agent orchestration skills with semantic Windows UI Automation. Use this instead of Remote Desktop Commander for heaven work unless the user explicitly authorizes Remote Desktop Commander.
